claims.statement: The UCI engine allows at most one active search; `go`, `ucinewgame` and `quit` first retire (cancel and settle) any active search, so the old search prints its bestmove before a new one starts.

Settling a search is guarded by a lock and a `settled` flag, so exactly one bestmove is printed per `go` regardless of races between the deadline timer, supervisor, stop and new commands; streamed analysis stops once a search is settled.

Search deadlines are None for infinite, ponder, or when neither movetime nor the side's clock is given; otherwise max(50, movetime-150) or max(50, min(remaining/(movestogo or 30)+increment, remaining)-150) ms, and expiry cancels the agent task.
Cancelled or failed searches still produce a bestmove; failures also emit `info string error: <message>`.

`go infinite` and `go ponder` searches are held: a finished result is not printed until `stop` or `ponderhit`; `ponderhit` converts the search to a normal one, settling immediately if done or arming a deadline otherwise; stop/ponderhit without an active held search are no-ops.

Completion rows are checked in order: a committed ply of the search's own request wins (even if cancelled), then resignation or other terminal outcome (bestmove 0000 with info reason), then a rejected position (bestmove 0000), then a fallback move.

The fallback move is the turn's `fallback_move` (System 1's top move) when the latest turn belongs to this request and the move is in the legal pool; otherwise a random choice from the pool seeded by `<Seed>:<request fingerprint>`, or 0000 when the pool is empty.
`bestmove 0000` is a null move rather than a standard UCI resignation and is intended to be scored as a forfeit by GUIs; fastchess (pinned at v1.8.2-alpha) scores it as an illegal-move loss.

When a fallback is played, the agent's turn remains pending; the GUI's next position includes the fallback, the core lifecycle marks the pending turn abandoned and syncs the fallback in as an external ply.

A game continues on the same thread only if the new position has the same normalized root FEN and its move list extends the checkpointed moves; takebacks, different roots, and `ucinewgame` start a new `uci-<uuid>` thread.
Illegal `searchmoves` are dropped with an info string, but the restriction is never widened: if all are illegal an empty restrict is sent and the agent rejects it with bestmove 0000.

The engine advertises case-insensitive options Model, ReasoningEffort (default/low/medium/high, where default maps to no effort), SystemOneModel, Policy, Threshold (0..1), K (1..255), Memory (none/summarize) and Seed (0..2^31-1), not Ponder; invalid or unknown options produce info strings and are ignored.

Option changes are queued during a search and applied after it settles (or at the next go / idle isready); when applied, the agent is rebuilt through the factory with the same checkpointer; isready always answers readyok immediately.
The UCI engine builds agents and run configs with draw_claims="never", leaving draw adjudication to the GUI.
`lcchess uci` runs the agent in-process over stdin/stdout with logging on stderr so stdout carries only protocol output; stdin is read in an executor and end of input is treated as quit.
UCI runs are traced as `chess-uci` with tag and metadata surface=uci plus all agent options and draw_claims.

`mise run test:uci` plays two games under fastchess between SemIf-only engines with seeds 1 and 2 (st=3, 60-move cap) and passes only if both games have a result and no termination other than normal or adjudication.
The `lcchess uci` command's `--memory` flag accepts only `none` (default) or `summarize`, and the command has no summary-trigger-tokens flag.

When the agent factory raises while applying queued options, the engine prints `info string options not applied: <error>`, discards the queue, and keeps the previous options and agent unchanged (e.g. Memory summarize refused for a model without a known input limit).

Replacing the UCI thread (on ucinewgame or a non-extending position) deletes the old thread from the checkpointer, only while no search is outstanding, so the checkpointer retains only the current game.
All `info string` output is produced by splitting text into one prefixed line per non-blank line, so multi-line agent text or error messages cannot forge UCI commands such as `bestmove` on stdout.
